cards.headline: White took the ko last, but Black has a local threat at D13 and White has none, so Black retakes for free: KO+, not KO−.

diagrams.caption: The tree's line. White 4 takes the ko, capturing Black 3, and the tree marks the leaf S[KO-].

No outside threats on either side. Black 5 ataris the white stone at C13, White 6 must capture, and Black 7 retakes without a threat elsewhere. White has no threat to retake with, so White 8 is played elsewhere, and Black 9 captures two stones and lives.
If White 6 connects instead, it is self-atari: Black 7 captures five stones and lives. Connecting at A12 fails the same way.

text: White 4 took the ko last, and the tree's KO− counts only that. But Black has a local ko threat and White has none. Black 5 in Diagram 2 ataris the lone white stone at C13, which has only two liberties on this 13×13 board. White 6 must capture: connecting is self-atari (Diagram 3), and ignoring Black 5 does not help White. Black 7 then retakes without spending a threat. After that, every local White move lets Black live, so White needs the first outside threat.

That is KO+: the solver finds that Black wins with as many threats as White and fails with one fewer. The site's tutorial gives this exact case as KO+: the opponent took first, but the player has a local threat and the opponent has none.

With a white stone on E13, Black has no threat, and the solver gives the tree's KO− (Diagram 4). If Kano's diagram has that stone, or a white wall along the top edge, the other fix is to add it and keep KO−. Otherwise fix this leaf together with leaf c056: on its own, this fix makes Black's first move at A10 correct too, tied at KO+ with the first move at A12.

cards.headline: Black has just taken the ko and still holds the local threat at D13, so White must win the ko twice: KO+2, not KO+.

diagrams.caption: The tree's line. Black 5 takes the ko, capturing White 2, and the tree marks the leaf S[KO+].

diagrams.moves: A11! D13 E13 A12 pass B13
diagrams.caption: White with one outside threat, Black with none. White 6 retakes after a threat elsewhere. Black 7 ataris C13, White 8 must capture, and Black 9 retakes without a threat. White has no threat left, so White 10 is played elsewhere, and Black 11 captures two stones and lives.

text: Black 5 has just taken the ko, and Black keeps the threat at D13. White 6 in Diagram 2 retakes with an outside threat, and the position is leaf c055, which is KO+. Then Black 7 ataris C13 and, as in leaf c055, White 8 must capture; Black 9 retakes for free. With only one threat more than Black, White has none left, and Black 11 captures two stones and lives.

So White must win the ko twice and needs two threats more than Black: KO+2, one step above leaf c055, as the tutorial's step-ko rule has it. The solver's counted searches agree: Black wins with one threat fewer than White and fails with two fewer. White has no local threat of its own: every local White move at the leaf lets Black live.

Fix both leaves together. With KO+2 here and KO+ on leaf c055, Black's first move at A12 stays the only correct answer, as the problem teaches; with KO+ on both, the first moves at A12 and A10 would tie. As with leaf c055, a white stone on E13 would make the tree's KO+ right, so if Kano's diagram has that stone, the other fix is to add it.
